name: Hoi An
provinceNote: Hoi An was in Quang Nam, which merged into Da Nang in 2025. Search and book it as Hoi An.
summary: Lanterns over the timber streets of a riverside trading town near Da Nang, with a covered Japanese bridge and the old town after dark. Walk it by day and on the 14th night of each lunar month, when the electric lights go off, visit the assembly halls and craft villages, swim at An Bang or walk the Tra Que herb gardens, and eat cao lau and white rose dumplings.
fee: 20,000 VND per person per building from 10 Aug 2026 (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). The heritage centre’s Jan and Mar 2026 notices still list 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND combination tickets. Ask at the booth which one it sells.
getThere: Fly into Da Nang (DAD), then about 30 km southeast by road, or bus route 02 from Da Nang central station.
seoTitle: Hoi An travel guide — lantern nights, the old town and An Bang
seoDescription: Lantern-hung timber streets 30 km southeast of Da Nang, the covered bridge, basket boats at Cẩm Thanh, and the sand at An Bang. Floods are usual from September to November.
intro: Come for the old town after dark: tiled timber shophouses with lanterns strung across the lanes, the covered wooden bridge at the west end, and the Thu Bồn the houses back onto. On the 14th night of each lunar month the town switches off its electric light for candles and lanterns. Walk it once in the morning and again at night, when the streets are pedestrian-only until 21:30 in summer and 21:00 in winter.

Sleep in the lanes just off the old town when the evening is the reason you came, and in Da Nang when the morning is the beach. An Bang, now in Hoi An Tây, is the Hoi An swim, with villas and homestays a ride from the old town. Erosion at Cửa Đại is serious, so swim at An Bang, though that coast is under threat too.

Tickets cover the old town’s houses, halls, and museums. From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor. The heritage centre’s 2026 notices still describe 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND combination tickets, so ask at the booth which one it sells that day.
gettingAround: Fly or take the train to Da Nang, then ride about 30 km southeast. From the Marble Mountains, the coast road along Trường Sa–Lạc Long Quân takes about 30 minutes.

Bus route 02 runs from Đà Nẵng central station through the Hoi An bus station to the inland-waterway parking at Cửa Đại, 05:30–18:00, every 20–30 minutes. Fares fall between 8,000 and 48,000 VND by distance and route, and pupils and students pay 8,000 VND.

Inside the old town, walk. The streets are pedestrian-only 09:00–21:30 in summer and 09:00–21:00 in winter, and Phan Châu Trinh, between Nguyễn Huệ and Cao Hồng Lãnh, joins them in the evening from 17:30, or from 15:00 under a 2023 plan. Cycle or take a ride to Trà Quế, about 2–2.5 km north, and to An Bang on the coast.

stayAreas.name: Old town edge
stayAreas.summary: The lanes just off the ancient-town core, so the lantern streets and the evening are a walk from your door.

stayAreas.name: An Bang
stayAreas.summary: Villas and homestays behind the sand, now in Hoi An Tây. The beach is outside the door; the old town at night is a ride back.

eat: Cao lầu is tossed while it is hot. People here call the noodles bánh. White rose dumplings are a small warm plate. Chicken rice is the lunch when you want a plate instead of noodles. Bánh mì is the morning stall in the old town. Bánh đập is the Cẩm Nam cracker, often with hến xào. Hoành thánh is the wonton. Nước mót is the herb drink.
Eat at the food hall inside Chợ Hội An by day. After dark, the night market runs along Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng.
interestsBody: Dining is cao lầu tossed while it is hot, white rose dumplings warm, bánh đập in Cẩm Nam, and chicken rice when you want a plate. Mì Quảng is the Quảng Nam bowl. The food guide is the first stop.

The night is the reason to sleep here: lanterns over the timber streets, the covered bridge at the west end, and on the 14th night of each lunar month, candles and lanterns in place of electric light.
Shop the old-town market by day for mắm cá cơm and gift cakes, walk the night market after dark, and cross to the craft villages for Thanh Hà clay and Kim Bồng carving.
An Bang is the swim and the villa stay, now in Hoi An Tây. Swim here rather than at Cửa Đại, where erosion is serious.
Cẩm Thanh is a basket-boat hour in the nipa palms, about 3 km from the old town.
Merchant houses such as Tấn Ký are the inside of the street: a shop at the front, the river at the back, and the family still upstairs.
The assembly halls are the Chinese merchant halls. Quảng Đông is the dragon court. Phúc Kiến is the long hall on Trần Phú. Chùa Ông is at 24 Trần Phú.
The museums are a morning hour: trade ceramics at 80 Trần Phú, Sa Huỳnh pottery at 149 Trần Phú, and the folk-culture house at 33 Nguyễn Thái Học.
Trà Quế is the herb village about 2–2.5 km north, where the greens on your cao lầu grow.
Kim Bồng is the carpentry village across the river. Thanh Hà is the pottery village west of town.
Resort living is Cua Dai when you want a pool morning and the old town at night.

body: The night is the reason to sleep in Hoi An. Lanterns hang over the timber streets, the shops stay open, and the covered bridge closes the view at the west end. The streets are pedestrian-only 09:00–21:30 in summer and 09:00–21:00 in winter, so walk the old town once in the morning and again after dark.

On the 14th night of each lunar month the town switches off its electric light for candles and lanterns. Local groups bring music, poetry, chess, martial arts, tuồng, bài chòi, and folk singing into the streets, and the night itself has no ticket.

Tickets cover the houses, halls, and museums. From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per person per building. The heritage centre’s 2026 notices still describe 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND combination tickets, so ask at the booth which one it sells.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: The old-town market by day, the night-market streets after dark, and clay and carving from the craft villages.

blocks.heading: Chợ Hội An
paragraphs: The yellow market hall sits inside the old town, with herb and vegetable sellers along the front and a food hall for cao lầu inside. Buy mắm cá cơm, the local anchovy sauce salted from fish off Cửa Đại and Cù Lao Chàm, and gift cakes such as bánh ú tro and bánh ít. Go in the daytime.

blocks.heading: The night market
paragraphs: After dark the stalls run along Nguyễn Hoàng, Công nữ Ngọc Hoa, Trần Quý Cáp, and Bạch Đằng, close to the old-town centre. Come for the local bowls and a slow walk between the lantern streets and the river.

blocks.heading: Thanh Hà clay
paragraphs: Thanh Hà, about 3 km west of the old town on the Thu Bồn, has made pots and tiles for more than 500 years, including the yin-yang roof tiles on the old houses. The small red clay animals are the thing to carry home.

blocks.heading: Kim Bồng wood
paragraphs: Kim Bồng sits on the south bank of the Thu Bồn, opposite the old town. The village has worked wood since about the 16th century in four trades: building timber, household wood, boats, and decorative carving. The carved heads are that last trade, and the village has been national intangible heritage since 2016.

blocks.heading: The silk village
paragraphs: Làng lụa Hội An, at 28 Nguyễn Tất Thành, was recognised as a local tourism site in 2018, on the same list as Kim Bồng and Thanh Hà.

cards.title: Hoi An Market
cards.summary: The yellow hall in the old town: herbs and vegetables out front, mắm cá cơm and gift cakes inside. A daytime stop.

cards.title: Thanh Hà pottery
cards.summary: Small clay animals from the village about 3 km west of the old town, the same trade that made the old-house roof tiles.

cards.title: Kim Bồng carving
cards.summary: Carved heads and decorative wood from the carpentry village across the river.

interestGroups.title: An Bang
interestGroups.summary: The Hoi An swim and the villa stay.

cards.title: An Bang Beach
cards.summary: Swim or walk the sand in front of the villa and homestay strip, now in Hoi An Tây. Give it a morning, or half a day when the swim is the point.

body: An Bang is the swim and the villa stay, now in Hoi An Tây. Swim here rather than at Cửa Đại, where erosion is serious, and know that this coast is under threat too.

interestGroups.title: Cam Thanh boats
interestGroups.summary: A basket-boat hour through the nipa palms.

cards.title: Cam Thanh Coconut Water
cards.summary: Take a basket boat through the nipa palms at Cẩm Thanh, about 3 km from the old town. Entry is 30,000 VND a person; the boat is extra. Bad weather can stop the boats.

body: Cẩm Thanh is a basket-boat hour in the nipa water, about 3 km from the old town. Entry is 30,000 VND from 10 August 2026, and the boat is paid separately.

interestGroups.summary: Palm Garden and Victoria on Cua Dai beach.

interestGroups.title: Merchant houses
interestGroups.summary: A tube house you can walk, with the shop at the front and the river at the back.

cards.title: Tan Ky House
cards.summary: A lived-in tube house at 101 Nguyễn Thái Học: the shop at the front, Chinese characters on the columns, and the river at the back. The family still lives upstairs, so the ground floor is the visit. Come in the morning.

cards.title: Phung Hung Old House
cards.summary: A timber house at 4 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, more than a hundred years old, with a Chinese balcony, a Japanese four-way roof on the middle bay, and a Vietnamese frame on eighty ironwood columns. The eighth generation still lives here.

cards.title: Quan Thang Old House
cards.summary: A one-storey merchant house more than 150 years old that runs through from Trần Phú to Nguyễn Thái Học. Kim Bồng carpenters cut the wood, and Chinese ceramics line the sky well.

blocks.heading: Shop at the front, river at the back
paragraphs: Merchant houses such as Tấn Ký are the inside of the street: a shop at the front, the river at the back, and the family still upstairs. The ground floor is the visit.

interestGroups.title: Assembly halls
interestGroups.summary: The Cantonese hall’s dragon court, the long Fujian hall, and Chùa Ông on Trần Phú.

cards.title: Cantonese Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The Cantonese merchants’ hall, built in 1885, with a pottery dragon in the court and a hall behind it. It began as a place for Thiên Hậu and Confucius; after 1911 the worship turned to Quan Công.

cards.title: Fujian Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The long hall at 46 Trần Phú, about 120 metres through three courts to the Thiên Hậu hall. It began in 1697 as Kim Sơn Tự and was rebuilt as the Fujian hall from 1757. If you enter one hall, make it this one.

cards.title: Chaozhou Assembly Hall
cards.summary: The Chaozhou hall at 157 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, built in 1845 for the gods of wind and wave. Carved wood and porcelain reliefs of folk stories, and quieter than the dragon court.

cards.title: Quan Cong Temple
cards.summary: The temple at 24 Trần Phú, built for Quan Công in the mid-17th century. The main hall holds the statue, two attendants, and two life-size horses. A short stop on the Trần Phú walk.

blocks.heading: The Hoa merchant halls
paragraphs: The assembly halls are the Chinese merchant halls. Quảng Đông is the dragon court. Phúc Kiến is the long hall on Trần Phú. Chùa Ông is at 24 Trần Phú.

interestGroups.title: Museums
interestGroups.summary: Trade ceramics, Sa Huỳnh pottery, and the folk-culture house. A morning hour.

cards.title: Museum of Trade Ceramics
cards.summary: A nineteenth-century tube house at 80 Trần Phú with 368 trade ceramics from the 9th to the 19th century. The house is the other exhibit: front, bridge, and back around a sky well. Closed on the 15th of each month.

cards.title: Sa Huynh Culture Museum
cards.summary: More than a thousand objects from the Sa Huỳnh culture, about two thousand years old, at 149 Trần Phú, with older pieces from Bãi Ông on Cù Lao Chàm. Closed on the 10th of each month.

cards.title: Museum of Folk Culture
cards.summary: A 57-metre house at 33 Nguyễn Thái Học that runs through to Bạch Đằng. Upstairs, 490 objects of folk art, performance, trades, and daily life; downstairs, craft demonstrations. Closed on the 20th of each month.

body: The museums are a morning hour: trade ceramics at 80 Trần Phú, Sa Huỳnh pottery at 149 Trần Phú, and the folk-culture house at 33 Nguyễn Thái Học.

interestGroups.title: Tra Que herbs
interestGroups.summary: The herb beds about 2–2.5 km north, where the greens on your cao lầu grow.

cards.title: Tra Que Vegetable Village
cards.summary: Walk the herb beds about 2–2.5 km north of the old town, where more than 20 leaf and herb crops grow, including the greens on cao lầu. Join a farmer hour, see two shrines and a stone well. Go in the morning.

body: Trà Quế is the herb village about 2–2.5 km north of the old town, between the Đế Võng river and the lagoon. The greens on your cao lầu grow here.

interestGroups.title: Craft villages
interestGroups.summary: Kim Bồng woodwork across the river, and Thanh Hà pottery west of town.

cards.title: Kim Bong Carpentry Village
cards.summary: The carpentry village on the south bank of the Thu Bồn, opposite the old town. Watch carvers and boatbuilders in a craft dating from about the 16th century, national intangible heritage since 2016. Go in the morning.

cards.title: Thanh Ha Pottery Village
cards.summary: The pottery village about 3 km west of the old town on the Thu Bồn, at the wheel for more than 500 years. Its kilns made the roof tiles on the old houses. Go in the morning.

blocks.heading: Across the river, and west of town
paragraphs: Kim Bồng is the carpentry village across the river. Thanh Hà is the pottery village west of town. Both are a morning by bicycle or a short ride.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Hoi An or Da Nang?
faqs.a: Sleep in Hoi An when the lantern streets after dark are the reason you came. Sleep in Da Nang when you want the beach in the morning. The old town is about 30 km southeast of Da Nang city.

faqs.q: What does the ancient-town ticket cost?
faqs.a: From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor. The heritage centre’s 2026 notices still describe 80,000 VND and 120,000 VND combination tickets. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale that day.
The 14th night of each lunar month, when the old town switches off electric light for candles and lanterns. The civil date moves every month, so check a lunar calendar for your dates.

faqs.q: Is Hoi An worth visiting in October?
faqs.a: Floods are usual from September to November, and the rainy season runs October to December. The town can be open and under water in the same month. If your dates are fixed, keep a Da Nang hotel as the backup and check the road that morning.

season.label: Flood risk Sep–Nov
season.note: January to September is the dry season and October to December the rainy one. Floods are usual from September to November, and storms mainly September to December. Check the Hoi An road on the morning you go.
